subject: Accounting
title: Special Purpose Entities
description: Learn Special Purpose Entities in one minute.

hook.text: Enron created hundreds of shell companies with names like Jedi, Chewco, and LJM.

buildup.text: These 'special purpose entities' were used to move debt off Enron's main balance sheet.

discovery.text: Billions in losses were hidden inside these entities. Enron's books looked clean.

twist.text: CFO Andrew Fastow personally profited by managing these entities—a massive conflict of interest.

climax.text: When the structures collapsed, all that hidden debt came crashing back onto Enron's books.

punchline.text: You can hide debt. You can't hide forever.

quiz.question: What were Enron's special purpose entities used for?
options: Hiding debt off the balance sheet

details.summary: Special purpose entities are separate legal structures created for specific business purposes. This topic explains how Enron and others used SPEs to move debt off the balance sheet, hide losses, and create the illusion of financial health.
details.whyItMatters: SPEs are legitimate business tools, but Enron showed they can be weaponized to deceive investors. Understanding SPE abuse is essential for evaluating corporate financial transparency.
takeaways: Enron created thousands of SPEs to hide debt and move losses off its financial statements
SPEs only needed 3% outside equity under pre-Enron rules—Enron exploited this low threshold
Post-Enron rules require consolidation of SPEs when the company bears the majority of risk

faq.question: What are special purpose entities?
faq.answer: Special purpose entities are separate legal structures created for a specific business purpose—like holding assets or isolating financial risk. They become problematic when companies use them to move debt off the balance sheet to make financial statements look healthier than reality.

faq.question: How did Enron use special purpose entities for fraud?
faq.answer: Enron created thousands of SPEs that it secretly controlled, transferring failing assets and debt to these entities to keep them off Enron's balance sheet. This made Enron appear less indebted and more profitable. When the SPEs couldn't sustain themselves, everything collapsed.
